calc.income-tax.note.ae: યુએઈમાં પગાર આવક પર કોઈ વ્યક્તિગત આવકવેરો નથી, તેથી હાથમાં આવતી રકમ કુલ પગાર જેટલી જ રહે છે.
calc.income-tax.note.ca: Federal tax, CPP and EI for 2026. Provincial income tax is not included and adds materially to the total.
calc.income-tax.note.au: 2026–27 Australian adult full-year resident, single without dependants. Resident bands0/15/30/37/45%, LITO, ordinary Medicare thresholds28,011/35,013 under current legislation as at22October2026; later retrospective changes not predicted. Enter lawful actual deductions; no automatic instant-deduction eligibility. Excludes SAPTO, family/exemptions, Medicare surcharge, HELP, super, other offsets and2027–28 WATO. Annual liability, not payslip withholding.
calc.income-tax.note.de: Tax class I for 2025 under the §32a schedule, with employee social contributions. Social contributions are not deducted as Vorsorgeaufwendungen, so the taxable income shown is higher than on a real assessment. Church tax is calculated separately.
calc.income-tax.note.at: 2025 rates with employee social insurance. Absetzbeträge are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.ch: Federal direct tax only. Cantonal and communal taxes usually exceed the federal amount and are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.fr: 2025 barème for a single share. The quotient familial for couples and dependants is not modelled.
calc.income-tax.note.be: 2025 rates including an indicative 7% communal surcharge. Regional differences are not modelled.
calc.income-tax.note.nl: 2026 ordinary wages only: full-year Netherlands resident below AOW age, fully covered by national insurance, with one wage source and no other income or deductions. Includes combined Box 1 rates and general/employment tax credits; aggregate income is assumed equal to wages. Excludes Box 2/3, expat treatment, pension/health deductions and special credits. Annual arithmetic estimates are not payslip withholding or a complete tax return.
calc.income-tax.note.jp: National tax, the 2.1% reconstruction surtax and a flat 10% resident tax, with employment income and basic deductions.
calc.income-tax.note.es: State scale plus an indicative regional scale for 2025. Your autonomous community's rates will differ.
calc.income-tax.note.mx: 2025 annual ISR tariff. The subsidio para el empleo is not included.
calc.income-tax.note.it: IRPEF for 2025 with indicative regional and municipal surcharges, which vary by comune.
calc.income-tax.note.pt: Mainland Portugal for 2025, single taxpayer without dependants.
calc.income-tax.note.br: IRPF annualised from the 2025 monthly table using the simplified deduction, plus INSS.
calc.income-tax.note.pl: Poland 2026: single resident, ordinary full-time employment, one local job and twelve near-equal payments. Annual contributory wages start at PLN57,672. Employee pension 9.76% and disability 1.5% share a PLN282,600 annual base cap; sickness 2.45% is uncapped. Health is 9% after those employee contributions. Monthly components round to grosz. Income/salary tools additionally deduct these social contributions and PLN3,000 employment costs, round the taxable base to PLN, apply 12/32% at PLN120,000 and the PLN3,600 tax reduction, then round PIT to PLN; gross wages limited to PLN1m. The standalone contribution tool excludes PIT. No joint filing, PIT-0 exemptions, other income, commuter costs, tax credits, PPK, employer contributions, sick pay or irregular/partial-year payments. Monthly outputs are annual averages, not payslips. The marginal percentage excludes monetary rounding steps.
calc.income-tax.note.tr: 2025 tariff with SGK and unemployment contributions. The minimum wage exemption is not applied.

calc.vat.note.ca: GST alone is 5%. HST provinces combine it with the provincial share into a single rate, and others charge PST or QST separately.
calc.vat.note.au: GST is 10% and applies to most goods and services, with basic food, health and education GST-free.
calc.vat.note.de: The standard rate is 19%, with 7% for food, books and public transport.
calc.vat.note.at: The standard rate is 20%, with reduced rates of 10% and 13%.
calc.vat.note.ch: The standard rate is 8.1%, with 2.6% for everyday goods and 3.8% for accommodation.
calc.vat.note.fr: The standard rate is 20%, with 10%, 5.5% and 2.1% applying to specific goods and services.
calc.vat.note.be: The standard rate is 21%, with 6% and 12% for specific categories.
calc.vat.note.nl: The standard rate is 21%, with a 9% rate for food, books, medicines and some services.
calc.vat.note.jp: Consumption tax is 10%, with a reduced 8% rate for food and drink other than alcohol and dining out.
calc.vat.note.es: The standard rate is 21%, with 10% and a super-reduced 4% for essentials.
calc.vat.note.mx: IVA is 16% nationally, with a reduced 8% rate in the northern and southern border regions.
calc.vat.note.it: The standard rate is 22%, with 10%, 5% and 4% applying to specific goods.
calc.vat.note.pt: Mainland rates are 23%, 13% and 6%. Madeira and the Azores use lower rates.
calc.vat.note.br: Brazil layers ICMS, ISS, PIS and COFINS rather than charging one VAT. These are common ICMS rates and are a rough guide only.
calc.vat.note.pl: The standard rate is 23%, with 8% and 5% for specific goods.
calc.vat.note.tr: KDV is 20% as standard, with 10% and 1% rates for specific goods.
calc.vat.note.ae: VAT is 5% on most goods and services, with some supplies zero-rated or exempt.
calc.capital-gains.title: કૅપિટલ ગેઇન ટૅક્સ કૅલ્ક્યુલેટર
calc.capital-gains.desc: રોકાણના નફા પરનો વેરો અને ચોખ્ખો નફો અંદાજો.
calc.capital-gains.note.us: Long-term rates apply after twelve months; shorter holdings are taxed as ordinary income. The 3.8% net investment income tax is not included.
calc.capital-gains.note.gb: UK 2026/27 resident individual ordinary chargeable gains only, assuming the full £3,000 annual exemption is unused elsewhere. Enter adjusted acquisition cost and net disposal proceeds after eligible costs. Taxable gains fill the unused £37,700 basic-rate band above your entered taxable income at 18%, then 24%. Holding duration does not change these rates. Excludes FIG/OWR claims, carried interest, business relief, losses, share matching, joint ownership allocation and exempt assets. This is not total annual liability or a reporting/deadline check.
calc.capital-gains.note.ca: Half the gain is taxable and added to income. The marginal rate used here is indicative and excludes provincial tax.
calc.capital-gains.note.au: Assets held over twelve months qualify for the 50% discount; the remainder is taxed at your marginal rate.
calc.capital-gains.note.de: Germany 2026, resident single private investor with ordinary taxable securities acquired after 2008 and no church tax. Enter adjusted acquisition cost, net disposal proceeds and the unused portion of your €1,000 saver allowance; zero means already used. Positive gain after this allowance is taxed at 25% plus solidarity surcharge of 5.5% of that tax (26.375% combined), regardless of holding time. Excludes losses, funds/partial exemptions, property, crypto, business/substantial holdings, joint assessment and foreign-tax credits. A lower-rate election may reduce actual liability; not calculated here. No refund or loss relief is calculated. This is a flat-rate illustration:26.375% applies before rounding. The25% income-tax component is displayed rounded to the nearest cent; solidarity is5.5% of the unrounded component with fractional cents discarded, then the displayed components are added. Bank withholding and final tax-assessment rounding are not modeled.
calc.capital-gains.note.fr: France: 2025 ordinary private securities gains assessed in 2026, single resident with full French social levies, default PFU only. Positive net proceeds minus adjusted cost: 12.8% income tax plus 18.6% social levies, regardless of holding time. Enter the higher total CEHR/CDHR reference income including the gain, up to €250,000. No progressive election, losses/carryforwards, PEA or employee schemes, special reliefs, foreign credits, crypto, property or business gains. Not for foreign social affiliation or high-income assessments. Estimate before collection thresholds and whole-return rounding; no refund or filing calculation.
calc.capital-gains.note.es: Spain 2026: ordinary resident in common territory, taxable savings-base gains. Enter adjusted acquisition cost, net disposal proceeds and other taxable savings income, not salary. Positive gain stacks above that savings base at 19%, 21%, 23%, 27% and 30%, with boundaries €6,000/50,000/200,000/300,000; holding time is irrelevant. Assumes the personal/family minimum is fully absorbed by the general base. Excludes loss offsets, minimum allocation, joint reductions, Basque/Navarre, Ceuta/Melilla, special exemptions and foreign-tax credits. Not a full return; no loss/refund calculation.
calc.capital-gains.note.it: Italy 2025: resident private individual, ordinary taxable securities gains within the 26% substitute-tax regime only. Enter adjusted acquisition cost and net disposal proceeds. A positive gain is taxed at 26% regardless of holding time. No loss offsets/carryforwards, preferential government bonds, funds, crypto, property, business or special holdings, foreign-tax credits, filing or payment calculation. A negative difference produces zero estimated tax, not a loss-relief or refund calculation.
calc.capital-gains.note.in: બાર મહિનાથી વધુ રાખેલી લિસ્ટેડ ઇક્વિટી પર ₹1.25 લાખથી ઉપરના નફા પર 12.5% વેરો લાગે છે; ઓછા સમયગાળા પર 20%.
calc.stamp-duty.title: Stamp Duty Calculator
calc.stamp-duty.desc: Work out the stamp duty land tax on a property purchase.
calc.stamp-duty.note: England and Northern Ireland residential SDLT from 1 April 2025, not Wales or Scotland. Includes standard bands, declared first-time relief up to £500,000, 5 percentage points for additional property and an optional 2 points for non-UK residents. You must establish buyer/relief/residency eligibility. Excludes linked transactions, lease rent, corporate buyers and special reliefs. The table shows base bands; surcharges are separate.

calc.church-tax.desc: Estimate the church tax charged alongside your income tax.
calc.church-tax.note: 8% in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, 9% in the other federal states. Leaving the church formally ends the liability.
calc.property-tax.title: Property Tax Calculator
calc.property-tax.desc: Multiply a taxable assessed value by the annual property-tax rate you enter.
calc.property-tax.note: Enter the taxable assessed value after applicable assessment adjustments and exemptions, and the annual percentage from your local authority. Zero percent is an editable placeholder, not an exemption. Annual amount = value × rate / 100; monthly amount = annual / 12; ten-year amount assumes both inputs stay unchanged. Example: 200,000 at 1.25% gives 2,500 per year. This does not value a property, supply local rates, decide eligibility, calculate credits or add fixed levies. Market price may differ from taxable assessed value. Country changes currency only.

calc.social-security-benefit.desc: Estimate your monthly Social Security retirement benefit.
calc.social-security-benefit.note: 2026 first-eligibility cohort (age 62 in 2026), full retirement age 67. Enter 12 times your already established average indexed monthly earnings, not current salary. Two bend points: $1,286 and $7,749; three rates: 90%, 32%, 15%. AIME is rounded down to dollars, PIA to dimes, adjusted monthly benefit to dollars. Ages 62/65/67/70 compare claiming factors in constant 2026 values, excluding later COLAs. No earnings-record indexing, eligibility determination, earnings test, family benefits, Medicare deductions or income tax. This is an illustration, not an SSA award.
calc.superannuation.title: Superannuation Calculator

calc.superannuation.note: Uses the 12% Superannuation Guarantee rate from 1 July 2025. Contribution caps and Division 293 tax are not modelled.
calc.hecs.title: HECS-HELP Calculator
calc.hecs.desc: See what your HELP debt costs each year and when it clears.
calc.hecs.note: Uses the selected {year} ATO repayment table. Enter repayment income, not salary alone: taxable income excluding assessable FHSS releases, reportable fringe benefits, net investment losses, reportable super contributions and exempt foreign employment income. Enter the current debt after any applicable debt reduction. The projection holds the selected table fixed, applies your indexation before repayment, floors each projected income to whole AUD and rounds annual repayments to cents. Future thresholds, actual indexation dates, eligibility, assessment rounding and refunds are not calculated.

calc.social-security.note: માત્ર કર્મચારીનો હિસ્સો. નોકરીદાતાનો ફાળો અલગથી લાગે છે અને અહીં બતાવ્યો નથી.
calc.national-insurance.title: National Insurance Calculator
calc.national-insurance.desc: Work out the National Insurance due on your earnings.
calc.national-insurance.note: 2026/27 annualised category A employee Class 1 NI: 8% above £12,570 to £50,270, then 2%. Assumes a full year and eligibility to pay. Employer NI, age exemptions, other categories, multiple employments and pay-period rounding are excluded. Monthly values are annual totals divided by 12, not exact payroll deductions.
calc.cpp.title: CPP Calculator
calc.cpp.desc: Calculate your Canada Pension Plan contributions.
calc.cpp.note: Scope: 2026 full-year employee CPP including CPP2 and EI outside Quebec, using annual pensionable/insurable earnings. It excludes QPP/QPIP, self-employment, employer contributions, partial years, age exemptions and pay-period rounding. Monthly amounts are annual totals divided by 12, not payslip withholding. Use CRA guidance for your employment situation.
calc.ei.title: EI Calculator
calc.ei.note: Scope: 2026 full-year employee CPP including CPP2 and EI outside Quebec, using annual pensionable/insurable earnings. It excludes QPP/QPIP, self-employment, employer contributions, partial years, age exemptions and pay-period rounding. Monthly amounts are annual totals divided by 12, not payslip withholding. Use CRA guidance for your employment situation.
calc.30-percent-ruling.title: 30% Ruling Calculator
calc.30-percent-ruling.desc: See what the Dutch 30% ruling is worth to you each year.
calc.30-percent-ruling.note: Netherlands 2026: assumes an approved ruling and employer agreement for the full year, the WNT cap applies, resident below AOW age with full national insurance, wages only. Enter the annual package including the allowance. Maximum tax-free amount is the lowest of 30% of the package, €78,600 and the amount leaving taxable wages strictly above €48,013 (or €36,497 for qualifying master’s graduates under 30 throughout the year). No 27% rate applies to this 2026 calculation. Excludes eligibility assessment, partial years, turning 30, pre-cap grandfathering, researchers/doctors, actual-cost election, Box 2/3 and pension/health deductions. Benefit compares modelled annual taxes/credits, not payslip withholding or guaranteed pay.

calc.severance-pay.note: Türkiye, ordinary eligible severance with at least one year of service. Select the half-year of termination (2025/2026); its ceiling applies to monthly gross remuneration including regular benefits. Gross severance = capped monthly remuneration × decimal service years; stamp duty is 0.759%. Notice pay is a separate gross illustration: monthly remuneration / 30 × 28 days up to 1.5 years, 42 days up to 3 years, then 56 days. calc.bmr.title: BMR Calculator

calc.tdee.title: TDEE & Calorie Calculator
calc.tdee.desc: Daily calories to maintain, lose or gain weight, with a macronutrient split.
calc.tdee.note: The macro split shown is a common 30/40/30 starting point, not a prescription. Anyone with a medical condition, or who is pregnant, should take dietary targets from a professional rather than a calculator.
calc.bodyFat.title: Body Fat Calculator
calc.bodyFat.desc: Estimate body fat percentage from tape measurements using the US Navy method.
calc.bodyFat.measureHint: In centimetres, or inches multiplied by 2.54.
calc.bodyFat.note: The circumference method has a stated error of roughly three to four percentage points, and depends heavily on measuring in the same place each time. Treat the trend as meaningful and any single reading as approximate.
calc.water.title: Water Intake Calculator
calc.water.desc: A daily water target from your body weight and how much you exercise.
calc.water.note: Roughly a fifth of most people's fluid comes from food, and needs rise in heat, at altitude and during illness. Thirst is a reasonable guide for healthy adults; this is a starting point, not a quota.
calc.pace.title: Running Pace Calculator
calc.pace.desc: Pace, speed and predicted finishing times from a distance and a time.
calc.pace.note: The race times assume you hold this exact pace throughout. In practice pace drifts over longer distances, so treat the marathon figure in particular as optimistic.
calc.statistics.title: Statistics Calculator

calc.statistics.listHint: Separate values with commas or spaces, e.g. 12, 15, 15, 18.
calc.statistics.sampleHint: Use this one when your numbers are a sample of a larger group.
calc.statistics.empty: Enter some numbers, separated by commas or spaces.

calc.ratio.scaleHint: Solves A : B = this : ? — useful for scaling a recipe or a mix.
calc.ratio.scaledHint: The second term at that scale.
calc.exponent.title: Exponent Calculator
calc.exponent.desc: Powers, roots and logarithms, with the inverse of each.
calc.exponent.rootHint: The nth root of the base.
calc.exponent.negativeNote: A negative base has a real root only for an odd degree; even roots of a negative number are not real, and are shown as a dash.
calc.quadratic.title: Quadratic Equation Calculator
calc.quadratic.desc: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0, with the discriminant and the turning point.
calc.quadratic.notQuadratic: With a = 0 this is not a quadratic but a straight line, which has at most one root.

calc.triangle.desc: Hypotenuse, area, perimeter and angles from the two shorter sides.

calc.area.note: Units are whatever you put in. Enter metres and the area is square metres; enter feet and it is square feet.
calc.volume.note: Units follow your input. A cubic metre is exactly 1,000 litres, which is what the last row converts.

calc.countryNote.units: Units default to what is used in {country}. You can switch them below.
calc.margin.title: Profit Margin Calculator
calc.margin.desc: Margin, markup and gross profit from a cost and a selling price.
calc.margin.lossNote: The selling price is below cost, so this is a loss rather than a margin.
calc.markup.title: Markup Calculator
calc.markup.desc: The price to charge to hit a target markup or margin on your cost.
calc.markup.note: Switching between markup and margin changes the price for the same percentage, which is exactly why the option is here rather than assumed.
calc.breakEven.title: Break-Even Calculator
calc.breakEven.desc: How many units you must sell to cover your fixed costs, and the revenue that takes.
calc.breakEven.note: Units are rounded up, because selling a fraction of one does not cover anything.
calc.breakEven.neverNote: Each unit costs at least as much to make as it sells for, so no volume breaks even — every extra sale widens the loss. Raise the price or cut the variable cost.
calc.roi.title: ROI Calculator
calc.roi.desc: Return on investment, in total and annualised.
calc.roi.note: This ignores tax, fees and inflation, all of which reduce a real return.
calc.roas.title: ROAS Calculator
calc.roas.desc: Return on ad spend, and the ROAS you actually need to break even.
calc.roas.marginHint: Your margin on the products sold, before advertising.
calc.roas.breakEvenHint: Below this, the campaign loses money.
calc.roas.note: A high ROAS on a thin margin can still lose money. The profit-after-ads row is the one that decides whether the campaign paid.
calc.growth.title: Growth Rate Calculator
calc.growth.desc: Total growth, compound annual growth rate, and the change between two figures.
calc.growth.averageHint: Shown for comparison; it overstates growth whenever the series compounds.
calc.growth.note: CAGR smooths the path completely. Two businesses with the same CAGR can have had very different years in between.
calc.discount.title: Discount Calculator
calc.discount.desc: The final price after a discount, and what you actually save.
calc.discount.extraHint: A second reduction applied to the already discounted price.
calc.discount.stackNote: Stacked discounts multiply rather than add: 20% off then a further 20% off is 36% off, not 40%.
calc.fuelCost.title: Fuel Cost Calculator
calc.fuelCost.desc: What a journey costs in fuel, in whichever units your car reports.
calc.fuelCost.note: Distance, economy and price must be in matching units — miles with gallons, kilometres with litres. Real consumption also varies with speed, load and traffic.
calc.electricity.title: Electricity Cost Calculator
calc.electricity.desc: What an appliance costs to run, per day, per month and per year.
calc.electricity.wattsHint: In watts — check the label or the manual.
calc.electricity.note: This assumes the appliance draws its rated power the whole time it is on. Anything thermostatic — a fridge, a heater, a kettle — cycles, so real consumption is lower.
calc.recipe.title: Recipe Scaler
calc.recipe.desc: Scale every ingredient in a recipe to the number of servings you need.
calc.recipe.amountHint: Any quantity from the recipe — grams, millilitres, whatever it uses.
calc.recipe.note: Ingredients scale; cooking times do not. A double batch in the same tin is deeper and takes longer, and seasoning is usually better scaled by taste than by arithmetic.
calc.gpa.title: GPA Calculator
calc.gpa.desc: Grade point average on the 4.0 scale, weighted by course credits.
calc.gpa.note: Courses with zero credits are ignored, so you can leave the slots you do not need. This uses the common US 4.0 scale; your institution's own scale may differ, and many weight honours or advanced courses higher.
calc.weightedGrade.title: Weighted Grade Calculator
calc.weightedGrade.desc: Your overall grade when assessments count for different amounts.
calc.weightedGrade.note: Assessments with zero weight are ignored, so unused slots can be left alone.
calc.weightedGrade.partialNote: Your weights add to {weight}%, not 100%. The grade shown is your average across only that part of the course — useful mid-term, but not your final standing.
calc.finalGrade.title: Final Grade Calculator
calc.finalGrade.desc: The mark you need on what is left to reach the grade you want.
calc.finalGrade.completedHint: The share of the total grade already assessed.
calc.finalGrade.note: This assumes the rest of the course is graded on the same percentage scale as what you have done so far.
calc.finalGrade.impossibleNote: That target needs more than 100% on what is left, so it is out of reach — the figure is shown as it is rather than capped, because a capped 100% would wrongly suggest it is still possible.
calc.concrete.title: Concrete Calculator
calc.concrete.desc: Concrete volume for a slab or footing, with bags and the mix breakdown.
calc.concrete.thicknessHint: In the same units as length and width — 0.1 m, or 0.33 ft for 4 inches.
calc.concrete.bagHint: What one bag makes up — roughly 0.011 m³ for a 25 kg bag, or 0.375 ft³ for an 80 lb bag.
calc.concrete.note: Units are whatever you entered — metres in, cubic metres out. The constituent split uses the standard 1.54 dry-volume allowance and is an estimate for ordering, not a mix design.
calc.paint.title: Paint Calculator
calc.paint.desc: How much paint a room needs, allowing for doors, windows and coats.
calc.paint.perimeterHint: Add up all four walls — for a 5 × 4 room that is 18.
calc.paint.openingsHint: Their total area, to subtract. A standard door is about 1.8 m².
calc.paint.coverageHint: From the tin — usually 10–14 m² per litre, or around 350 sq ft per gallon.
calc.paint.note: Coverage falls on porous or previously unpainted surfaces, and a strong colour change may need an extra coat. Buying slightly over is usually cheaper than a second trip for a part-tin.
calc.tile.title: Tile Calculator
calc.tile.desc: Tiles and boxes needed for a floor or wall, including cutting waste.

review.scope.india: TY2026–27: resident below60, salary only; Act2025 sections19/156/202. Standard deduction75000 new/50000 old, ordinary slabs/rebate/surcharge relief and4% cess. Only independently eligible entered old-regime deductions. No special/foreign/agricultural income, EPF or other payroll charges, payslip or final return/payment rounding.
review.scope.canada: 2026 scope: federal income-tax bands and basic personal credit, plus annual employee CPP/CPP2 and EI outside Quebec. Provincial tax, other federal credits and payroll-period withholding are excluded.
review.scope.401k: Review scope: elective deferral, matching, combined contribution and eligible compensation limits. Catch-up contributions are excluded.
review.scope.socialSecurity: 2026 first-eligibility cohort (age 62 in 2026), full retirement age 67. Enter 12 times your already established average indexed monthly earnings, not current salary. Two bend points: $1,286 and $7,749; three rates: 90%, 32%, 15%. AIME is rounded down to dollars, PIA to dimes, adjusted monthly benefit to dollars. Ages 62/65/67/70 compare claiming factors in constant 2026 values, excluding later COLAs. No earnings-record indexing, eligibility determination, earnings test, family benefits, Medicare deductions or income tax. This is an illustration, not an SSA award.
review.scope.hecs: Uses the selected 2026–27 / 2025–26 ATO repayment table. Enter repayment income, not salary alone: taxable income excluding assessable FHSS releases, reportable fringe benefits, net investment losses, reportable super contributions and exempt foreign employment income. Enter the current debt after any applicable debt reduction. The projection holds the selected table fixed, applies your indexation before repayment, floors each projected income to whole AUD and rounds annual repayments to cents. Future thresholds, actual indexation dates, eligibility, assessment rounding and refunds are not calculated.
review.health.bmi: The CDC reference describes adult BMI screening categories. BMI is not a diagnosis or a weight prescription; these adult bands are not for children or pregnancy.
review.health.energy: This resting-energy model is for adults aged 18 or over, not children, pregnancy or breastfeeding. The study describes resting energy expenditure in healthy adults. Activity multipliers and calorie or macro targets are planning assumptions, not measurements validated by that study.
review.health.water: This weight-and-exercise calculation is a rough illustration, not an EFSA recommendation or a drinking quota. EFSA reference values include food and all beverages. Fluid restrictions, illness, pregnancy and endurance exercise need individual advice.
comparison.loan.title: Compare the cost of changing one assumption
comparison.loan.intro: These illustrations start with the worked-example inputs above. Each other row changes only the named input; all remaining inputs stay at the example values. They do not update when you edit the calculator.
comparison.loan.scope: The comparison holds the interest rate fixed throughout each scenario. A shorter term can increase the monthly payment while reducing total interest. A larger down payment reduces borrowing at the same purchase price; it also requires more cash upfront.
comparison.loan.apr: The entered rate is a nominal annual interest rate divided by 12, not an APR that includes fees. Compare lender documents, charges and repayment conditions separately. The CFPB reference below explains this distinction for US mortgages; it does not verify local lending rules.
calc.mortgage.costs: The loan amount is the property price minus the percentage down payment. The result covers principal and interest only. Property taxes, insurance, mortgage insurance, closing costs and maintenance can increase the monthly housing budget. Total payable here excludes the down payment and those additional costs.
calc.loan.rateAssumption: Starting rates are illustrative assumptions, not current market rates or offers. This model assumes equal end-of-month repayments, monthly interest and no rate changes. Enter the terms of the actual loan; payment holidays, daily interest and income-contingent repayments require a different model.
validation.adultEnergy: This resting-energy model is for adults aged 18 or over, not children, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
validation.energyTarget: This tool cannot provide a suitable calorie target for these inputs. Targets below 1,000 kcal/day and weight-loss targets for an underweight adult are withheld. This threshold is not a recommended intake. Ask a qualified health professional for individual advice.
calc.vat.rateHint: Enter the rate applicable to your transaction. The starting 0% is an editable placeholder, not a tax exemption or a national rate.
calc.vat.scope: This tool adds or removes one percentage that you supply: tax = net × rate / 100; net = total / (1 + rate / 100). For example, net 100 at 20% gives tax 20 and total 120; reversing total 120 gives net 100. It does not determine which tax applies, registration, exemptions, recoverability, compounded taxes or filing obligations. Check the rate, location, product and effective date with the relevant tax authority. Country selection changes currency and the tax name, not the applicable law.
calc.pension.scope: This is a private savings illustration using your salary, employee/employer contribution percentages and a constant return. Default percentages are examples, not legal minimums or employer commitments. It does not calculate a state pension, eligibility, statutory limits, tax relief or fees. Salary and contributions are constant; returns and inflation can change. The displayed 4% withdrawal is only a scenario, not guaranteed sustainable income.
review.scope.canadaContributions: Scope: 2026 full-year employee CPP including CPP2 and EI outside Quebec, using annual pensionable/insurable earnings. It excludes QPP/QPIP, self-employment, employer contributions, partial years, age exemptions and pay-period rounding. Monthly amounts are annual totals divided by 12, not payslip withholding. Use CRA guidance for your employment situation.
calc.projection.timing: Projection convention: the entered annual percentage is divided by 12 and compounded monthly for both the existing balance and deposits. Monthly deposits enter at the start of each month. Salary, deposits and the assumed rate stay constant; actual returns are not guaranteed.
review.scope.usIncome: 2026 US resident, one wage earner, under 65 and not a dependent. Joint filing assumes the spouse has no income. Includes ordinary federal wage bands, standard or entered itemised deduction, Social Security and Medicare. Excludes state/local taxes, credits, AMT, NIIT and special deductions. This estimates annual liability, not employer withholding or a complete tax return.
review.scope.ukIncome: 2026/27 England, Wales and Northern Ireland; not Scotland. Includes ordinary income bands, the personal allowance taper and annualised Class 1 employee NI or Class 4 in self-employed mode. For self-employment enter profit after business expenses, not sales. No savings/dividends, pension/Gift Aid relief, tax-code adjustments, age exemptions or payroll-period rounding. Salary results are annual estimates, not payslips.
review.scope.ukNI: 2026/27 annualised category A employee Class 1 NI: 8% above £12,570 to £50,270, then 2%. Assumes a full year and eligibility to pay. Employer NI, age exemptions, other categories, multiple employments and pay-period rounding are excluded. Monthly values are annual totals divided by 12, not exact payroll deductions.
review.scope.uaeWages: 2026 employment wages only: no UAE personal income tax is modelled, and wages are not natural-person corporate-tax business turnover. This is not a business/corporate tax calculation. Pension, insurance, other payroll deductions and taxes owed to other countries are excluded; the result is not a guaranteed bank receipt.
review.scope.russiaWages: 2026 ordinary Russian resident wages: progressive NDFL bands of 13%, 15%, 18%, 20% and 22%. It does not calculate investment/property income, nonresident or special-rate income, regional allowances, employer contributions or other wage deductions. Enter only deductions whose eligibility and limits you have independently established. Annual tax is rounded to the nearest whole ruble; 50 kopecks rounds up. Monthly outputs are annual averages, not payroll-period withholding. The marginal band rate excludes rounding steps.
review.scope.sdlt: England and Northern Ireland residential SDLT from 1 April 2025, not Wales or Scotland. Includes standard bands, declared first-time relief up to £500,000, 5 percentage points for additional property and an optional 2 points for non-UK residents. You must establish buyer/relief/residency eligibility. Excludes linked transactions, lease rent, corporate buyers and special reliefs. The table shows base bands; surcharges are separate.
calc.stamp-duty.residencyHint: Use the specific SDLT residence test, not nationality or ordinary income-tax residence. Check HMRC guidance before selecting.
calc.property-tax.scope: Enter the taxable assessed value after applicable assessment adjustments and exemptions, and the annual percentage from your local authority. Zero percent is an editable placeholder, not an exemption. Annual amount = value × rate / 100; monthly amount = annual / 12; ten-year amount assumes both inputs stay unchanged. Example: 200,000 at 1.25% gives 2,500 per year. This does not value a property, supply local rates, decide eligibility, calculate credits or add fixed levies. Market price may differ from taxable assessed value. Country changes currency only.
review.scope.usFica: 2026 employee FICA on one person’s annual covered wages, single filing: Social Security 6.2% up to $184,500, Medicare 1.45% plus 0.9% above $200,000. This is annual liability, not employer withholding. Excludes employer/self-employed shares, joint spouse wages, exemptions, income/state taxes and benefit eligibility. Monthly figures divide the annual total by 12.
review.scope.auWages: 2026–27 Australian adult full-year resident, single without dependants. Resident bands0/15/30/37/45%, LITO, ordinary Medicare thresholds28,011/35,013 under current legislation as at22October2026; later retrospective changes not predicted. Enter lawful actual deductions; no automatic instant-deduction eligibility. Excludes SAPTO, family/exemptions, Medicare surcharge, HELP, super, other offsets and2027–28 WATO. Annual liability, not payslip withholding.
calc.salary.scope: The result subtracts only the taxes and contributions included in this model. It is not a complete payslip or a promise of the amount reaching your bank account. Check the tax period and exclusions beside the result; provincial or local tax, other payroll deductions, benefits and individual credits can change actual pay.
field.severanceMonthlyGross: Monthly gross remuneration including regular benefits
review.scope.trSeverance: Türkiye, ordinary eligible severance with at least one year of service. Select the half-year of termination (2025/2026); its ceiling applies to monthly gross remuneration including regular benefits. Gross severance = capped monthly remuneration × decimal service years; stamp duty is 0.759%. Enter the eligible service fraction yourself; this tool does not establish entitlement, dates, breaks or special-contract treatment. Notice pay is a separate gross illustration: monthly remuneration / 30 × 28 days up to 1.5 years, 42 days up to 3 years, then 56 days. It is not automatically due, is not added to the main result and excludes notice income tax and stamp duty. Check contractual terms and legal eligibility.
review.scope.nlWages: 2026 ordinary wages only: full-year Netherlands resident below AOW age, fully covered by national insurance, with one wage source and no other income or deductions. Includes combined Box 1 rates and general/employment tax credits; aggregate income is assumed equal to wages. Excludes Box 2/3, expat treatment, pension/health deductions and special credits. Annual arithmetic estimates are not payslip withholding or a complete tax return.
field.taxableOtherIncome: Other taxable income after allowances and reliefs
calc.capital-gains.ukIncomeHint: Enter taxable income excluding this gain, after the Personal Allowance and eligible income-tax reliefs. Do not enter gross salary here.
review.scope.ukGains: UK 2026/27 resident individual ordinary chargeable gains only, assuming the full £3,000 annual exemption is unused elsewhere. Enter adjusted acquisition cost and net disposal proceeds after eligible costs. Taxable gains fill the unused £37,700 basic-rate band above your entered taxable income at 18%, then 24%. Holding duration does not change these rates. Excludes FIG/OWR claims, carried interest, business relief, losses, share matching, joint ownership allocation and exempt assets. This is not total annual liability or a reporting/deadline check.
review.scope.chContributions: Switzerland, 2026: ordinary insured employee below reference age, one job for the full year. Enter remuneration already subject to contributions, including applicable bonuses. Employee AHV/IV/EO is 5.3%; ALV is 1.1% up to CHF 148,200. This does not determine liability, small-wage exemptions, partial-year caps or multiple-job treatment. Employer-exempt cases, occupational pension, accident/health insurance, income tax and benefits are excluded. Monthly = annual / 12, not a payslip.
review.scope.ptContributions: Portugal, 2026 ordinary employee regime: employee contribution is 11% of entered annual contributory remuneration. Include subject holiday/Christmas allowances and bonuses. Employer contributions and IRS are excluded. Not for self-employed people, directors, domestic workers, special classes, exemptions, reduced rates or conventional bases. Does not determine benefit entitlement. Monthly = annual / 12, not the deduction on each of 14 salary payments.
review.scope.deGains: Germany 2026, resident single private investor with ordinary taxable securities acquired after 2008 and no church tax. Enter adjusted acquisition cost, net disposal proceeds and the unused portion of your €1,000 saver allowance; zero means already used. Positive gain after this allowance is taxed at 25% plus solidarity surcharge of 5.5% of that tax (26.375% combined), regardless of holding time. Excludes losses, funds/partial exemptions, property, crypto, business/substantial holdings, joint assessment and foreign-tax credits. A lower-rate election may reduce actual liability; not calculated here. No refund or loss relief is calculated. This is a flat-rate illustration:26.375% applies before rounding. The25% income-tax component is displayed rounded to the nearest cent; solidarity is5.5% of the unrounded component with fractional cents discarded, then the displayed components are added. Bank withholding and final tax-assessment rounding are not modeled.
review.scope.itGains: Italy 2025: resident private individual, ordinary taxable securities gains within the 26% substitute-tax regime only. Enter adjusted acquisition cost and net disposal proceeds. A positive gain is taxed at 26% regardless of holding time. No loss offsets/carryforwards, preferential government bonds, funds, crypto, property, business or special holdings, foreign-tax credits, filing or payment calculation. A negative difference produces zero estimated tax, not a loss-relief or refund calculation.
review.scope.esGains: Spain 2026: ordinary resident in common territory, taxable savings-base gains. Enter adjusted acquisition cost, net disposal proceeds and other taxable savings income, not salary. Positive gain stacks above that savings base at 19%, 21%, 23%, 27% and 30%, with boundaries €6,000/50,000/200,000/300,000; holding time is irrelevant. Assumes the personal/family minimum is fully absorbed by the general base. Excludes loss offsets, minimum allocation, joint reductions, Basque/Navarre, Ceuta/Melilla, special exemptions and foreign-tax credits. Not a full return; no loss/refund calculation.
field.frReferenceIncome: Higher total CEHR/CDHR reference income (including gain)
calc.capital-gains.frReferenceHint: Enter the higher of total RFR and adjusted CDHR reference income, including this gain, not wages alone. This single-person model supports at most €250,000.
calc.capital-gains.frReferenceError: Reference income must include the gain and be at least as large as it.
review.scope.frGains: France: 2025 ordinary private securities gains assessed in 2026, single resident with full French social levies, default PFU only. Positive net proceeds minus adjusted cost: 12.8% income tax plus 18.6% social levies, regardless of holding time. Enter the higher total CEHR/CDHR reference income including the gain, up to €250,000. No progressive election, losses/carryforwards, PEA or employee schemes, special reliefs, foreign credits, crypto, property or business gains. Not for foreign social affiliation or high-income assessments. Estimate before collection thresholds and whole-return rounding; no refund or filing calculation.
review.scope.plEmployment: Poland 2026: single resident, ordinary full-time employment, one local job and twelve near-equal payments. Annual contributory wages start at PLN57,672. Employee pension 9.76% and disability 1.5% share a PLN282,600 annual base cap; sickness 2.45% is uncapped. Health is 9% after those employee contributions. Monthly components round to grosz. Income/salary tools additionally deduct these social contributions and PLN3,000 employment costs, round the taxable base to PLN, apply 12/32% at PLN120,000 and the PLN3,600 tax reduction, then round PIT to PLN; gross wages limited to PLN1m. The standalone contribution tool excludes PIT. No joint filing, PIT-0 exemptions, other income, commuter costs, tax credits, PPK, employer contributions, sick pay or irregular/partial-year payments. Monthly outputs are annual averages, not payslips. The marginal percentage excludes monetary rounding steps.

Maximum tax-free amount is the lowest of 30% of the package, €78,600 and the amount leaving taxable wages strictly above €48,013 (or €36,497 for qualifying master’s graduates under 30 throughout the year). No 27% rate applies to this 2026 calculation. Excludes eligibility assessment, partial years, turning 30, pre-cap grandfathering, researchers/doctors, actual-cost election, Box 2/3 and pension/health deductions. Benefit compares modelled annual taxes/credits, not payslip withholding or guaranteed pay.

review.root.usGains: US 2026, single resident under 65, ordinary private securities and standard deduction only. Other ordinary AGI must absorb the $16,100 deduction; combined AGI ≤$500,000. Long term means more than one year, stacked at 0/15/20%; short term uses ordinary brackets. Includes 3.8% NIIT over $200,000. No other gains, dividends, losses, credits, AMT preferences or state/local tax. Federal estimate before return rounding.
review.root.caGains: Canada 2026: federal tax only, ordinary private securities, 50% inclusion for every holding period. Enter other net taxable income after deductions. Other income plus the full gain ≤CAD181,440; no other AMT adjustments. Applies basic personal credit only. No provincial tax, Quebec abatement, other credits, losses, registered accounts or special exemptions. This is additional federal tax, not the total Canadian liability.
review.root.auGains: Australia 2026–27: resident under 65, single, no dependants, ordinary shares acquired after 21 September 1999, resident throughout ownership. Long term means eligible ownership of at least 12 months for 50% discount. Adds the taxable gain above other taxable income with LITO and ordinary Medicare levy. Assumes adequate private hospital cover. No other gains/losses, HELP, SAPTO, foreign residency, indexation or special concessions. Current-law Medicare thresholds as at22October2026; later retrospective changes not predicted. No disposals on/after1July2027 or proposed future reforms.
review.root.inGains: India TY2026–27: new-regime resident, eligible STT-paid listed equity/equity funds only. Long term means more than 12 months: 12.5% above the fully unused ₹125,000 annual threshold; short term 20%; both plus 4% cess. Other taxable ordinary income must be at least ₹1,300,000 and total including gain ≤₹5,000,000. No other gains/losses, surcharge, rebate, property, unlisted or debt assets; supply adjusted cost after any grandfathering.
review.root.nlPayroll: Netherlands 2026: full-year ordinary fully insured private-sector employee. Select actual AWf contract and Aof employer categories. Enter actual combined Whk assessment rate and employer pension/other costs; no national average is inferred. Statutory premiums include WKO and Zvw, capped at €79,409 annual premium wage. Holiday allowance is included in the base. No self-insurers, public-sector, special exemptions or part-year calculation. Employer cost only, excluding employee net-pay computation.
review.root.auSuper: Australia2026–27: covered employee18–66, TFN supplied, taxed accumulation fund, no other income/funds; qualifying earnings before salary sacrifice ≥AUD45,000. SG12% on annual earnings up toAUD270,830; total SG+sacrifice ≤AUD32,500, no carry-forward. Includes15% fund tax and Division293 assumed paid from fund. No LISTO at this income. Return after tax/fees; monthly beginning deposits. Current contributions/rules stay fixed in projection; future law, payday compliance/receipt timing, benefits, withdrawals and Division296 excluded. Growth aboveAUD3million has no additional earnings tax modeled.
review.scope.deEmployment2025: Germany 2026: single, childless age 23+, outside Saxony, ordinary GKV employee with sickness benefits, twelve equal payments above €2,000 each. Enter the actual unchanged supplementary fund rate. Monthly contribution caps/cent rounding, deductible pension/96% health/care, €1,230 employment costs and €36 special-expense allowance; basic income tax and solidarity phase-in. No church tax, joint filing, other income/reliefs, private insurance, mini/midijobs, bonuses or part years. The contribution tool excludes income tax. Monthly amounts are annual averages, not payslips.
review.scope.atEmployment2025: Austria 2026: ordinary ASVG employee under 60, one job, twelve equal regular payments, annual gross at least €40,000. Monthly contribution base capped at €6,930, component cent rounding, €132 employment costs and €496 transport credit. No 13th/14th salary, special payments, other income/reliefs, commuting/family credits, e-card charge or refunds. The contribution tool excludes income tax. Monthly amounts are annual averages, not payslips. Outside Vienna only; Vienna housing contributions are excluded.
review.scope.chFederal2025: Switzerland 2026: single full-year resident, ordinary federal assessment only. Supply final federal taxable income after independently established deductions, not gross wages. Base rounds down to CHF100; tax below CHF25 is not collected. Salary also deducts AHV/IV/EO 5.3%, ALV 1.1% up to CHF148,200, and your actual other employee deductions. No cantonal, municipal, church or wealth taxes, health premiums, married/parent tariff, source withholding or part years. This does not determine deduction eligibility or total take-home pay. Salary scope: fully covered employee below reference age, annual contributory pay above CHF2,500. Annual federal tax rounds down to CHF0.05.
review.scope.deChurch2025: Germany 2026: ordinary full-year church member. Enter the final church-tax assessment base under §51a, which is adjusted income tax, not income. Ordinary surcharge: 8% in Bavaria/Baden-Württemberg, 9% elsewhere. Excludes capital-income special rules, church-specific caps/minima, special church payment, joint/mixed-faith allocation, reliefs and income-tax deduction benefit; not a complete assessment.
review.scope.atChurch2026: Vienna Roman Catholic church, 2026: single employee/pensioner, ordinary full-year income contribution. Enter assessed taxable income for 2025 and the separate tax-favoured special-pay base: 1.1% minus €61 plus 0.5% of special pay, at least €35 overall. No family/discretionary relief, other dioceses, self-employment, assets, non-taxable additions, support allocations, fees or income-tax deduction benefit.
review.scope.chChurch2025: City of Zurich, Reformed church, 2026: ordinary full-year member income-tax surcharge, 10% of assessed simple cantonal income tax. The base is not income or total cantonal/municipal tax. Excludes wealth-related church tax, mixed-faith allocation, limited liability, other denominations and municipalities; not total Swiss church liability.
review.scope.dePayroll2025: Germany 2026: ordinary private employer liable to insolvency levy, employee age 23–59 outside Saxony, twelve equal payments above €2,000. Capped employer pension/unemployment/health/care shares, monthly component rounding and 0.15% insolvency levy. Supply actual unchanged fund supplement, applicable U1/U2 rates and annual accident/other employer costs. U1 can be zero for an exempt employer. No mini/midijobs, bonuses, public-employer exemptions, special occupations or benefit calculations. Monthly cost is an annual average.

review.scope.asia.tr: Türkiye 2026: one ordinary resident employee, twelve equal full-month wages from TRY 396,360/year. SGK 14% and unemployment 1%, monthly base capped at TRY 297,270.00; deduct these before the wage tax bands (third threshold TRY 1.5m). Apply the monthly minimum-wage income-tax exemption and 0.759% stamp tax above the minimum wage. No bonuses, partial years, pensioners, reliefs, other income or BES. Monthly output is an annual average; not a payslip. Private-sector regular wage withholding totals only; annual return settlement is excluded.
review.scope.asia.br: Brazil 2026 annual assessment: single resident, twelve equal regular wages from BRL 19,452/year, no dependants or other income. Monthly progressive INSS is capped at BRL 8,475.55. Use the official 2026 annual IRPF table and the larger of modeled INSS or the 20% simplified deduction (maximum BRL 17,640.00), without double deduction. No 13th salary, vacation extra, irregular pay, other itemized deductions, credits or withholding/refund settlement. Monthly output is the annual assessment average. Annual2026 wage-only reduction: tax zero up to gross BRL60,000; from60,000.01 through88,200, subtract up to BRL8,429.73−0.095575×gross, capped at tax; none above88,200. No other income/dividends.
review.scope.asia.cn: China 2026: full-year resident wage-only annual IIT, RMB 60,000 expense deduction and national 3–45% bands. Enter actual eligible employee social/housing-fund payments and other verified deductions from records; no assumed city rates. Contributions reduce both taxable income and cash wages. Excludes nonresidents, separately taxed bonuses, other income, reliefs, foreign credits and withholding/refund settlement. Annual average after tax and entered contributions; not a complete payslip.
review.scope.asia.jp: Japan 2026: resident, wages only, no dependants, credits or other income. NATIONAL income tax plus 2.1% reconstruction levy; revised 2026 salary-income table and basic deduction apply. Enter actual annual social premiums; taxable income floors to JPY 1,000 and reconstruction levy to JPY 1. No premature JPY 100 final-balance rounding. Local resident tax is not inferred from national income: salary tool only subtracts entered actual assessed local tax. No current-year local-tax prediction, final withholding/refund settlement or full payslip. 2026 annual year-end provisions effective1December2026; excludes earlier death/departure quasi-final returns.
review.scope.asia.mx: Mexico 2026: resident, fully taxable wages only, twelve equal months from MXN 180,000/year, above the monthly employment-subsidy limit. Official SAT annual fixed-fee/lower-limit ISR tariff; no personal deductions. Enter actual employee IMSS: subtract it from cash wages, not again from the ISR base. No flat2.775% estimate. Excludes exempt benefits, minimum-wage exemption, bonuses, other income, annual withholding/refund settlement and employer shares. Annual average after modeled deductions, not a payslip. Twelve equal monthly wages must exceed2026 subsidy limit MXN11,492.66 and both minimum-wage zones; annual input minimum MXN180,000.
review.scope.asiaSocial.tr: Türkiye 2026 employee contributions only: twelve equal full months, annual contributory wages at leastTRY396,360. SGK 14% plus unemployment 1%, shared monthly base cap TRY 297,270.00, components rounded monthly to kuruş. No income/stamp taxes, employer shares, pensioners, partial months or benefits.
review.scope.asiaSocial.br: Brazil 2026: one full month, ordinary employee/domestic/avulso INSS only. Progressive7.5/9/12/14% bands at BRL 1,621/2,902.84/4,354.27/8,475.55; only each slice is charged and top base caps contributions. No 13th salary, employer share, other jobs, self-employment, benefits or IRPF.
review.scope.asiaSocial.jp: Tokyo Kyokai Kenpo, April–December 2026, one full month, ordinary insured employee age 20–64. Enter separately assessed health/pension standard monthly grades, not assumed current cash pay. Employee health 4.925% (5.735% at 40–64 including care), pension 9.15%, general-industry unemployment 0.5% of insured wages; payroll half-yen ties round down. No bonuses, other insurers/prefectures, eligibility assessment, exemptions or taxes. Not a full-year 2026 estimate. April–December2026 only: employee child-support0.115% of assessed health base is shown separately; not an annual estimate.
review.scope.asiaSocial.cn: Beijing, July–December 2026, one full ordinary employee month. Enter assessed prior-year average monthly wage; statutory base floor RMB 7,270/cap 36,348. Employee pension 8%, health 2% plus RMB 3, unemployment 0.5%; each component to fen. Housing fund is excluded. No employer shares, other cities, flexible employment, retirees, income tax or benefits. Not a full-year 2026 estimate.
review.scope.asiaSocial.mx: Mexico 2026 ordinary IMSS employee, daily registered integrated SBC from MXN 500 (above both minimum wages),1–31 calendar contribution days. January UMA 113.14, February–December 117.31; SBC cap 25 UMA. Employee components0.25/0.375/0.625/1.125% of SBC plus 0.4% only above 3 UMA. Components rounded to cents for entered days; agency monthly/bimonthly grouping can differ by cents. No employer share, minimum-wage employer-paid quota, ISSSTE, absence rules, INFONAVIT loans, wages or ISR.
